introduction: In competitive exams (SSC, Railways, Police), questions frequently look beyond Microsoft Windows to test your awareness of alternative operating systems. At this foundational level, we define what 'Open-Source' means and explore the world's most popular free operating systems.

core_concepts.title: Open-Source Software
core_concepts.description: Software whose underlying 'Source Code' is made completely free for the public to view, modify, and distribute. Anyone can customize it according to their needs. Unlike Windows, which is proprietary, open-source software promotes community collaboration.

core_concepts.title: Linux OS
core_concepts.description: The world's most famous open-source operating system, created in 1991 by 'Linus Torvalds'. It is highly secure and dominates the world of web servers, mainframes, and supercomputers. Its official mascot is an adorable penguin named 'Tux'.

core_concepts.title: Android OS
core_concepts.description: Developed primarily by Google, Android is the world's most popular mobile operating system, custom-built for touchscreen smartphones and tablets. It is also an open-source project (AOSP).

core_concepts.title: The Android-Linux Connection
core_concepts.description: A premier exam fact: The Android operating system is built on top of the 'Linux Kernel'. In simple terms, underneath Android's custom visual interface lies a core Linux engine.

important_entities.name: Linus Torvalds
important_entities.significance: He started Linux as a free hobby project while at university; today, his creation powers almost the entire global internet infrastructure.

important_entities.name: macOS & iOS
important_entities.significance: Designed exclusively for Apple hardware (MacBooks and iPhones). They are strictly closed-source (Proprietary) and commercial.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Many candidates assume that because a cracked or free ISO of Windows can be downloaded from the internet, Windows is open-source. This is incorrect. Windows is Proprietary (requires a paid license). Linux is genuinely 100% free and legally open-source.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Android is just Linux in a Mobile suit
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Whenever an exam question asks about the base, foundation, or kernel of Android, immediately select 'Linux'.

exam_strategy_tips: Differentiating proprietary vs. open-source is a favorite Tier-1 topic. In 'Find the Odd One Out' questions, if you see Windows, macOS, iOS, and Linux grouped together, Linux is the answer because it is the only open-source OS among them.
